summary_paraphrase: A boy reading with his grandmother asks whether giraffes or lions live on the hill outside; she says no and takes him to see what does, and on the walk they meet a dassie, a hare and birds before he finds a golden stone she calls a tiger's eye.

beats.function: reading together, hill in the window

characters.name: Luvo
characters.desire: to know which animals live on the hill
characters.fear: a hint: whether a lion hides there
characters.goal: to see the hill for himself
characters.change: from storybook animals to the real animals and a treasure of his own hill

characters.name: Makhulu
characters.desire: to show him his own place

humor_notes: Almost none; one visual pun on the stone's name (tiger's eye) on page 11.

repetition.description: two rounds of a storybook-animal question answered with a gentle no
repetition.why: the second round is predictable, so the break into 'let's go and see' lands as a turn

repetition.description: Luvo's call to his grandmother to look returns on the dassie and stone pages
repetition.why: marks his two own discoveries; the second one is the peak

repetition.description: the title phrase returns as the last line
repetition.why: closes the book on its own name

notes: The animals Luvo imagines (giraffe, lion) are drawn as his own soft toys sitting on a rock; the real animals are drawn in a different, naturalistic way.
The window frame of page 1 returns on page 5 with the two hands reaching across it: inside turns to outside.
Pages 8-9 are quiet: whispered and soft speech, few figures, open white space before the stone peak.
The page 11 picture puns on the stone's name with a tiger's eye in leaves.

strengths: imagined animals are answered by real ones: the child's own place becomes the wonder
a gentle question-and-no cycle that breaks into action
the peak is the child's own find, named by the grandmother
weaknesses: no problem to solve: stakes are curiosity only
the grandmother initiates the walk; the child's agency is in noticing

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: A lion is wondered about and calmly ruled out before the walk; no peril. Picking up a stone on a walk with a grandparent.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
